finding.claim: Unauthenticated /fetch2 route fetches any http/https URL supplied in the query string; only a scheme check guards the request, and the first 200 bytes of the response are returned to the caller.
finding.sink: views.py:22 requests.get(url, timeout=5) with redirects enabled

trace.note: is_http_url checks only urlparse(url).scheme in (http, https); no host, IP, or DNS check
requests.get(url, timeout=5) — no host check, redirects followed by default, body returned

finding.guards_checked: Scheme-only check (validators.py:6-7). No hostname allowlist, no IP-range denylist, no DNS-resolution check, no redirect re-validation. Scheme-only checks do not close SSRF per ssrf/SKILL.md.

verdict.guard_found: none. views.py:20 applies only is_http_url, and validators.py:6-7 checks only urlparse(url).scheme in ("http", "https"). No hostname, IP, or DNS check and no auth decorator on /fetch2 (views.py:17-18). The stricter is_safe_url guard (validators.py:10-18) is used only by /fetch at views.py:12, not by /fetch2.
verdict.reason: The source is request.args.get("url") at views.py:19 on an unauthenticated route, the only gate is the scheme-only is_http_url at views.py:20 / validators.py:7, and requests.get(url, timeout=5) at views.py:22 follows redirects by default and returns the first 200 bytes of the body.

finding.claim: /fetch validates the resolved IP of the hostname, then the HTTP client resolves the hostname again, so DNS rebinding can bypass the IP denylist and reach internal addresses.

trace.note: socket.getaddrinfo(parsed.hostname, ...) — first DNS resolution at check time
ip.is_private / is_loopback / is_link_local / is_reserved checks; returns False if any address matches
requests.get(url, ...) performs an independent second DNS resolution at use time; redirects disabled

finding.guards_checked: Scheme restricted to http/https (validators.py:12); hostname required (validators.py:12); every resolved address checked against private/loopback/link-local/reserved (validators.py:15-17); allow_redirects=False (views.py:14). Not closed: check-time and use-time resolutions are separate, so a TTL-0 rebinding record can return a public IP to the check and an internal IP to the fetch. Possible gap not verified: is_private may not cover 100.64.0.0/10.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. validators.py:12 (scheme and hostname presence) and validators.py:14-17 (per-address IP checks at check time) are not closing guards. views.py:14 allow_redirects=False only blocks redirects, not DNS rebinding. No pinned-IP connection or hostname allowlist exists anywhere in the path.
verdict.reason: Source is attacker-controlled (views.py:11) and nothing closes the check-to-use gap (validators.py:14 resolves at check time, views.py:14 resolves again inside requests.get), so the substance holds; but the trace misdescribes validators.py:15 as the is_private/is_loopback checks when it is the ip_address parse, and those checks are at validators.py:16-17, so the trace as submitted is wrong and should be corrected to validators.py:16-17 and resubmitted. The 100.64.0.0/10 gap was not verified and is not needed for the finding.
